title: Proving Conjectures of Ashoke Sen: F-Theory Limits, Small Black Holes and Dyon Indices
description: The paper examines thirty-six statements of Ashoke Sen on duality, dyon indices, tachyon condensation, F-theory and black hole entropy, and decides which are proved, which are supported but unproved, and where each stops. It proves that every weak coupling degeneration of F-theory on an elliptic Calabi-Yau variety is, after base change and rescaling, Sen's family, and that one exists exactly when -2K_B has a section; and that the entropy of a two-charge small black hole is fixed by one critical value for every curvature-corrected action, so that the Gauss-Bonnet truncation matches the statistical entropy only in four and five dimensions and Prester's Lovelock completion is the unique one that matches it in every dimension. Exact product expansions reproduce the negative full dyon indices of the toroidal orbifolds, with thirty negative-index charge triples in the scanned cone. For the complete heterotic action in six or more dimensions, which is not a claim of Sen, it proves that the central-charge route does not give the statistical value under its own hypotheses; the statement remains open. Three highlights mark what Sen got wrong, what is fatal and what is left unproved; no statement examined is wrong as printed or fatal. The archive holds the compiled paper, its LaTeX source, the exact-arithmetic program that computes every table, the Lean 4 certificates of the finite statements, and the scripts that check the explicit constants and the identities of the appendices.
